meter.gloss: to put in; to tuck in

meanings.en: to put in; to tuck in
meanings.note: Everyday Spanish verb specifically for putting something inside a pocket, bag, or drawer.

examples.text: Meto las llaves en el bolsillo.
examples.trans: I put the keys in my pocket.

examples.text: Metimos las sillas dentro por la lluvia.
examples.trans: We brought the chairs inside because of the rain.

meanings.note: Before an adjective (bien caliente), means 'nice and hot'.

examples.trans: Everything is going very well today.
The tea comes out nice and hot.

meanings.note: Forms: ese, esa, esos, esas.

examples.trans: Pass me that blue notebook.

examples.text: Esa maleta pertenece a un cliente.
examples.trans: That suitcase belongs to a guest.

esquina.gloss: corner (outer street corner or cake corner)

meanings.en: corner (outer street corner or cake corner)
meanings.note: Outer corner where two streets meet, or the crisp corner of a baking tray.

examples.trans: The corner is here.

examples.text: Vemos las esquinas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the corners from the door.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.
The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Sábanas limpias = clean sheets.

examples.trans: The bedsheet is here.

examples.text: Vemos las sábanas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the bedsheets from the door.

meanings.note: Right where the speaker is.

examples.trans: Here is your key.

examples.text: Nos sentamos aquí bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We sit right here under the tree.

meanings.note: Ir a + infinitive expresses near future ('going to do').

examples.text: Voy a abrir la puerta ahora.
examples.trans: I am going to open the door now.
How is everything going this morning?

meanings.note: Used with feminine plural nouns and clock hours (las ocho).

examples.trans: The windows face the garden.
We have breakfast at eight.

meanings.note: Los dos / las dos means 'both'.

examples.text: Pongo dos tazas azules en la mesa.
examples.trans: I put two blue cups on the table.

examples.text: Compra las dos válvulas por favor.
examples.trans: Buy both valves, please.

meanings.note: Soft bed pillow.

examples.trans: The pillow is here.

examples.text: Vemos las almohadas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the pillows from the door.

meanings.note: Opposite of duro (hard).

examples.trans: It is a soft piece.

examples.text: ¡Y yo tengo dos almohadas blandas y una alfombra azul en el almacén!
examples.trans: And I have two soft pillows and a blue rug in the storeroom!

meanings.note: With estar, means 'ready / all set'; with ser, means 'smart'.

examples.text: El té caliente ya está listo.
examples.trans: The hot tea is ready now.
She is a very smart architect.

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.
It is quarter past seven.

meanings.note: From Hispanic Arabic al-ḥánbal.

examples.trans: The rug is here.

examples.text: Vemos las alfombras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the rugs from the door.

meanings.note: Plural azules; azul marino means 'navy blue'.

examples.trans: It is a blue piece.

examples.text: Espere, ¡es azul oscuro, igual que la suya!
examples.trans: Wait, it is dark blue, just like yours!

meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg quepo and preterite cupe.

examples.text: La maleta cabe en el armario.
examples.trans: The suitcase fits in the closet.
Four more tables fit here.

meanings.note: Justo aquí = right here; justo al lado = right next door.

examples.trans: The key is right here.

examples.text: La panadería queda justo al lado.
examples.trans: The bakery is right next door.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition a + masculine article el; al + infinitive means 'upon doing'.

examples.text: Vamos al mercado por la mañana.
examples.trans: We go to the market in the morning.

examples.text: Al abrir la puerta, sonó el timbre.
examples.trans: Upon opening the door, the bell rang.

meanings.note: Al lado = on the side / next door.

examples.trans: The side is here.

examples.text: Vemos los lados desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the sides from the door.

meanings.note: Hacer la cama = to make the bed.

examples.trans: The bed is here.

examples.text: Vemos las camas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the beds from the door.

meanings.note: Interrogative adverb with written accent.

examples.text: Mira dónde señala con el lápiz.
examples.trans: Look where he is pointing with his pencil.

examples.text: ¿Dónde van las cucharillas y las servilletas?
examples.trans: Where do the teaspoons and the napkins go?

colgar.gloss: to hang; to hang up (the phone)

meanings.en: to hang; to hang up (the phone)
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: cuelgo) and g -> gu in preterite 1st sg (colgué).

examples.text: Cuelgo el abrigo detrás de la puerta.
examples.trans: I hang my coat behind the door.

examples.text: Colgó los farolillos entre las ramas.
examples.trans: He hung the lanterns among the branches.

meanings.note: Forms: este (m sg), esta (f sg), estos (m pl), estas (f pl).

examples.trans: This courtyard is very quiet.
This morning it is very sunny.

meanings.note: Wall or bathroom mirror.

examples.trans: The mirror is here.

examples.text: Vemos los espejos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the mirrors from the door.

meanings.note: Una mesa redonda = a round table.

examples.trans: It is a round piece.

examples.text: ¿Dónde cuelgo este espejo redondo? ¿A la izquierda de la ventana o a la derecha?
examples.trans: Where do I hang this round mirror? Left of the window or right?

meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: A la izquierda = on/to the left.

examples.trans: The left is here.

examples.text: Vemos las izquierdas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the lefts from the door.

meanings.note: Una ventana soleada = a sunny window.

examples.trans: The window is here.

examples.text: Vemos las ventanas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the windows from the door.

meanings.note: Becomes u before words starting with o- or ho-.

examples.trans: Do you prefer coffee or hot tea?
Do we open today or wait until tomorrow?

meanings.note: A la derecha / a mano derecha = on the right.

examples.trans: The right is here.

examples.text: Vemos las derechas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the rights from the door.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition de + masculine article el.

examples.text: El bizcocho acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The cake just came out of the oven.
I am a neighbour from the quarter.

meanings.note: Writing desk in a room or study.

examples.trans: The desk is here.

examples.text: Vemos los escritorios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the desks from the door.

meanings.note: Unaccented in relative clauses; accented dónde in questions.

examples.text: Esta es la plaza donde compramos flores.
examples.trans: This is the square where we buy flowers.
Sit where you feel most comfortable.

meanings.note: Impersonal present form hay means 'there is / there are'; haber que + infinitive = must / need to.

examples.text: Hay pan caliente en la cocina.
examples.trans: There is warm bread in the kitchen.
We have already prepared the rooms.

meanings.note: Shortens to buen before masculine singular nouns (buen viaje); ¡Buenos días! = Good morning!

examples.trans: Good morning, everyone!
The weather is very nice today.

meanings.note: Plural las luces; a plena luz del sol = in bright sunlight.

examples.trans: The light is here.

examples.text: Vemos las luces desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the lights from the door.

meanings.note: Built from enchufe (plug/socket).

examples.text: Enchufo la cafetera en la cocina.
examples.trans: I plug in the coffee maker in the kitchen.

examples.text: Enchufó la lámpara junto al sillón.
examples.trans: He plugged in the lamp beside the armchair.

meanings.note: Table, ceiling, or reading lamp.

examples.trans: The lamp is here.

examples.text: Vemos las lámparas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the lamps from the door.

meanings.note: Yellow copper-zinc alloy used for keys, lamps, and valves.

examples.text: El latón es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The brass is very important here.
We talk about the brass.

meanings.note: Expresses surprise, sympathy, or mild dismay.

examples.trans: Oh, I nearly forgot my umbrella!
Goodness, what a fright you gave me!

mirar.gloss: to look; to look at; to watch

meanings.en: to look; to look at; to watch
meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'at' (mira el reloj = look at the clock).

examples.text: Mira qué sol hace esta mañana.
examples.trans: Look how sunny it is this morning.

examples.text: Miramos el mapa antes de salir.
examples.trans: We look at the map before going out.

qué.gloss: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)

meanings.en: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)
meanings.note: Used in questions (¿qué hora es?) and exclamations (¡qué alivio!).

examples.trans: What time is it right now?
What a bright morning!

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number with its noun.

examples.trans: It is a yellow piece.

examples.text: ¡Acaba de parar un taxi amarillo frente a la verja de hierro!
examples.trans: A yellow taxi just pulled up outside the iron gate!

meanings.note: Shortened form of tanto used before adjectives and adverbs (¡qué mañana tan luminosa!).

examples.trans: What a peaceful courtyard!

examples.text: ¿Por qué sale el agua tan fría?
examples.trans: Why is the water running so cold?

meanings.note: Describes warm sound, light, or hospitality.

examples.trans: It is a warm piece.

examples.text: Enchufa la lámpara de latón de Mateo... ¡ay, mira qué luz amarilla tan cálida!
examples.trans: Plug in Mateo's brass lamp... oh, look how warm that yellow light is!

meanings.note: Formed from sincera + -mente.

examples.trans: Honestly, the sponge cake is delicious.
I mean it very sincerely.

meanings.note: Placed before the word it modifies.

examples.trans: It is almost twelve o'clock already.

examples.text: Casi olvido la llave en la mesa.
examples.trans: I nearly forgot the key on the table.

meanings.note: Sin querer = by accident; querer decir = to mean.

examples.trans: Would you like coffee or hot tea?
I opened it by accident.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue in present: duermo; o -> u in preterite 3rd: durmió).

examples.trans: I sleep eight hours every night.
Last night I slept wonderfully here.

meanings.note: Often omitted in Spanish unless adding contrast or emphasis.

examples.text: Yo abro la puerta y tú llevas la linterna.
examples.trans: I will open the door and you carry the flashlight.
It is me, please open up.

meanings.note: Agrees with the noun it describes.
In ahora mismo, meaning right now, mismo strengthens the time word ahora. Now comes from ahora; mismo supplies emphasis without agreeing with a person in this expression.

examples.trans: We have the same job.
I am busy right now.

meanings.note: Opposite of abajo.

examples.trans: The bedrooms are upstairs.
Look up toward the balcony.

meanings.note: ¡Buenas noches! = Good evening / Good night; esta noche = tonight.

examples.trans: The night is here.

examples.text: Vemos las noches desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the nights from the door.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: De momento = for now.

examples.trans: The moment is here.

examples.text: Vemos los momentos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the moments from the door.

meanings.note: Reduction in price.

examples.trans: The discount is here.

examples.text: Vemos los descuentos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the discounts from the door.

meanings.note: Third-person singular indirect object pronoun.

examples.text: Le llevo una taza de té caliente.
examples.trans: I am bringing you/her a cup of hot tea.
Do you like the courtyard room?

meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg ofrezco.

examples.text: Ofrecemos té caliente y fruta fresca.
examples.trans: We offer hot tea and fresh fruit.

examples.text: El vecino nos ofreció su escalera.
examples.trans: The neighbour offered us his ladder.

por.gloss: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)

meanings.en: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)
meanings.note: Por la mañana = in the morning; por favor = please; gracias por = thanks for.

examples.trans: We stroll through the old quarter.

examples.text: Por la mañana entra mucho sol.
examples.trans: In the morning plenty of sun comes in.

cambiar.gloss: to change; to swap; to exchange

meanings.en: to change; to swap; to exchange
meanings.note: Cambiar de habitación/camisa uses de before the noun.

examples.trans: I change the towels every morning.
We moved the table to a new spot.

meanings.note: Plural habitaciones.

examples.trans: The room is here.

examples.text: Vemos las habitaciones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the rooms from the door.

meanings.note: A mitad de precio = at half price.

examples.trans: The half is here.

examples.text: Vemos las mitades desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the halves from the door.

meanings.note: A mitad de precio = at half price.

examples.trans: The price is here.

examples.text: Vemos los precios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the prices from the door.

meanings.note: Con desayuno incluido = with breakfast included.

examples.trans: The breakfast is here.

examples.text: Vemos los desayunos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the breakfasts from the door.

meanings.note: Invariable as adverb or adjective.

examples.text: El mapa de la ciudad es gratis.
examples.trans: The city map is free.

examples.text: Los niños entran gratis al museo.
examples.trans: Children enter the museum for free.

meanings.note: Todo el día = the whole day; todo el mundo = everyone; sobre todo = mostly.

examples.text: Todo está limpio y en su sitio.
examples.trans: Everything is clean and in its place.

examples.text: Camina todo recto por esta calle.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead down this street.

meanings.note: Fin de semana = weekend; la semana que viene = next week.

examples.trans: The week is here.

examples.text: Vemos las semanas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the weeks from the door.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number.

examples.trans: It is a generous piece.

examples.text: ¡Qué generoso! ¿Habéis oído el timbre de la puerta del patio abajo?
examples.trans: How generous! Did you two hear the courtyard gate bell downstairs?

meanings.note: Irregular: oigo, oyes, oye, oímos, oís, oyen; ¡Oiga! / ¡Oye! gets someone's attention.

examples.trans: Can you hear me clearly on the phone?

examples.text: Acabo de oír pasos en la escalera.
examples.trans: I just heard footsteps on the stairs.

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.
Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Tocar el timbre = ring the bell.

examples.trans: The bell is here.

examples.text: Vemos los timbres desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the bells from the door.

meanings.note: Covers room doors, street doors, and courtyard gates.

examples.trans: The door is here.

examples.text: Vemos las puertas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the doors from the door.

meanings.note: Traditional inner courtyard at the heart of a Spanish building.

examples.trans: The courtyard is here.

examples.text: Vemos los patios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the courtyards from the door.

meanings.note: Indicates position or movement downward.

examples.trans: The kitchen is downstairs.

examples.text: Te espero abajo en el patio.
examples.trans: I will wait for you downstairs in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Las ocho = eight o'clock.

examples.text: Abrimos la puerta a las ocho.
examples.trans: We open the door at eight.
The guesthouse has eight rooms.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

punto.gloss: dot; point (en punto = on the dot; a punto de = about to)

meanings.en: dot; point (en punto = on the dot; a punto de = about to)
meanings.note: A las nueve en punto = at nine o'clock sharp.

examples.trans: The dot is here.

examples.text: Vemos los puntos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the dots from the door.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number with the thing possessed (nuestro patio, nuestra posada).

examples.trans: Our guesthouse has eight rooms.
Our neighbours have coffee here.

meanings.note: Can take el or la, alongside dedicated feminine clienta.

examples.trans: The guest is here.

examples.text: Vemos los clientes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the guests from the door.

meanings.note: ¡Ya está! = All done!; ya no = no longer.

examples.trans: Breakfast is already ready.
Coming right now with the keys!

meanings.note: Pairs with locations (está en el patio) and temporary states (está caliente).

examples.trans: Breakfast is ready now.
Where are the brass keys?

meanings.note: First-person singular object/reflexive pronoun.

examples.trans: Can you pass me the salt, please?
I live here and I work here.

meanings.note: El corazón me late rápido = my heart is beating fast.

examples.text: El corazón me late rápido de alegría.
examples.trans: My heart beats fast with joy.

examples.text: Sentía latir el pulso tras correr.
examples.trans: She felt her pulse beating after running.

meanings.note: Plural corazones.

examples.trans: The heart is here.

examples.text: Vemos los corazones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the hearts from the door.

meanings.note: A mil = racing at a thousand an hour.

examples.text: Gracias mil veces por tu ayuda.
examples.trans: Thanks a thousand times for your help.

examples.text: El corazón me va a mil.
examples.trans: My heart is racing at a thousand an hour.

meanings.note: Preterite 1st sg spells c -> qu: expliqué.

examples.text: Te explico el camino en un minuto.
examples.trans: I will explain the way to you in a minute.

examples.text: El arquitecto explicó toda la historia en el patio.
examples.trans: The architect explained the whole story in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Takes 3rd-person singular verbs (¿quiere usted...?).

examples.trans: What is your name?

examples.text: Pase usted por aquí, por favor.
examples.trans: Come this way, please.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: suena).

examples.text: El despertador suena a las seis y media.
examples.trans: The alarm clock rings at six thirty.

examples.text: El piano sonaba cálido bajo la lluvia.
examples.trans: The piano sounded warm in the rain.

meanings.note: Said alone to reassure someone ('Easy, don't worry!').

examples.trans: It is a quiet piece.

examples.text: Seca, calentita y tranquila. Ahora decidme qué falta.
examples.trans: Dry, warm, and quiet. Now tell me what is missing.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number.

examples.trans: It is a honest piece.

examples.text: Señor, antes de subir, le debo una disculpa sincera.
examples.trans: Sir, before going upstairs, I owe you an honest apology.

meanings.note: Dejar de + infinitive means 'to stop doing something'.

examples.text: Dejo las llaves en el mostrador.
examples.trans: I leave the keys on the counter.
Let me help you with that box.

meanings.note: Accented pronoun after para, por, a, de, sin (distinct from possessive mi).

examples.text: Esta taza de té es para mí.
examples.trans: This cup of tea is for me.
Leave it to me, please.

dar.gloss: to give; to face onto (dar a); to strike (the hour)

meanings.en: to give; to face onto (dar a); to strike (the hour)
meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg doy and preterite di/dio; dar las doce = strike twelve.

examples.text: La ventana da al patio soleado.
examples.trans: The window looks out onto the sunny courtyard.

examples.text: El reloj acaba de dar las doce.
examples.trans: The clock has just struck twelve.

meanings.note: Agrees with the person welcomed (bienvenido, bienvenida, bienvenidos, bienvenidas).

examples.trans: It is a welcome piece.

examples.text: Déjemelo a mí. Vamos abajo a darle la bienvenida.
examples.trans: Leave it to me. Let us go down and welcome him.

nos.gloss: us; to us; each other (¡Nos vemos!)

meanings.en: us; to us; each other (¡Nos vemos!)
meanings.note: First-person plural object/reflexive/reciprocal pronoun.

examples.trans: See you tomorrow morning!
The news makes us very glad.

meanings.note: Irregular: veo, vi, visto.

examples.text: Desde aquí veo el puente de piedra.
examples.trans: From here I see the stone bridge.
See you later in the courtyard!
